notes: Canonical UCI HAR dataset paper. 30 volunteers (age 19-48) performing 6 activities: WALKING, WALKING_UPSTAIRS, WALKING_DOWNSTAIRS, SITTING, STANDING, LAYING. Device: Samsung Galaxy S II, waist-mounted. Sensors: 3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyroscope, sampled at 50 Hz. Raw signals filtered (median + 3rd-order low-pass Butterworth 20 Hz cutoff); gravity separated from body acceleration via Butterworth low-pass at 0.3 Hz. Windowed into 2.56 s frames (128 readings) with 50% overlap -> 561-feature vectors (time + frequency domain). Data randomly split by subject: 70% train (21 subjects) / 30% test (9 subjects). Baseline result: multiclass one-vs-all Gaussian-kernel SVM ~ 96% overall test accuracy; main confusion between sitting and standing. The engineered 561-D feature set and the fixed train/test subject split are the standard 'UCI HAR' benchmark. Dataset DOI (UCI): https://doi.org/10.24432/C54S4K (recommended dataset citation: Reyes-Ortiz, Anguita, Ghio, Oneto, Parra 2013, UCI Machine Learning Repository). A follow-up 'HAPT' version adds 6 postural-transition classes and raw inertial signals. Note: the ESANN proceedings paper itself has no DOI; doi field left empty (dataset DOI recorded here).
